title: Fraud and Scams: Prevention, Detection and Response
summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on preventing, detecting and responding to fraud and scams, from authorised push payment scams and deepfakes to reimbursement and board reporting.
intro: This training programme equips fraud, payments operations and compliance teams to prevent, detect and respond to fraud and scams: assessing risk, deploying monitoring and customer interventions, protecting vulnerable customers and evidencing effective controls to supervisors.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip practitioners with a clear understanding of how modern fraud and scams work, from authorised push payment scams to deepfakes and insider fraud, and the controls that stop them. Participants leave able to assess fraud risk, tune detection, design effective customer interventions, handle reimbursement and redress fairly, and report meaningfully to the board.
sections.What It Covers: The fraud and scams landscape, authorised push payment and investment scams, account takeover and identity fraud, synthetic identities and deepfakes, insider and first-party fraud, fraud risk assessment, transaction monitoring and behavioural analytics, customer warnings and vulnerable customers, reimbursement and redress, data sharing and board reporting.
Intended Audience: Fraud prevention, fraud operations and investigations teams
Payments operations, customer service and complaints staff who handle suspected fraud cases
Compliance, financial crime and risk staff, and managers accountable for fraud outcomes
Learning Objectives: Explain how the main fraud and scam typologies work and why they succeed
Assess the firm's fraud risk across products, channels and customer groups
Design detection using transaction monitoring, behavioural analytics and identity controls
Apply effective customer warnings and interventions, especially for vulnerable customers
Handle reimbursement, redress and data sharing fairly and consistently
Evaluate fraud governance and management information, and agree an improvement plan
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a three- to four-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a short briefing with typology case studies and practical exercises, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's products and payment channels.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of fraud, payments operations or financial crime compliance is helpful. No technical background in data analytics is required.
Core Reading: FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
CPMI, Fast Payments: Enhancing the Speed and Availability of Retail Payments (2016)

modules.title: The Fraud and Scams Landscape
modules.summary: How fraud has shifted from unauthorised to authorised and socially engineered losses, who the perpetrators are, and why fraud is now a conduct, financial crime and resilience risk.
objectives: Distinguish unauthorised fraud, authorised scams, insider and first-party fraud
Explain the organised crime and technology drivers of current fraud trends
Identify the firm's obligations and exposures arising from fraud losses
syllabus: Fraud taxonomy: unauthorised, authorised, insider and first-party
Organised crime, fraud-as-a-service and money mule networks
Links between fraud, money laundering and consumer harm
Measuring losses: what the numbers show and conceal

modules.title: Authorised Push Payment and Investment Scams
modules.summary: How criminals persuade customers to send money themselves, from impersonation and romance scams to fake investment platforms, and the points at which firms can intervene.
objectives: Recognise the stages and psychology of authorised push payment scams
Identify investment, crypto-asset and impersonation scam patterns
Map intervention points across the payment journey
syllabus: Impersonation, purchase, romance and invoice redirection scams
Investment and crypto-asset scams, cloned firms and fake platforms
Social engineering, coaching and why customers override warnings
Case studies: tracing a scam from first contact to cash-out

modules.title: Account Takeover, Synthetic Identity and Deepfakes
modules.summary: How criminals take over genuine accounts or create fictitious customers, including the use of synthetic identities, deepfake audio and video, and AI-generated documents.
objectives: Explain account takeover methods, including phishing, SIM swap and malware
Recognise synthetic identity and document forgery at onboarding
Assess identity verification and authentication controls against deepfake attacks
syllabus: Credential theft, SIM swap, remote access and device compromise
Synthetic identities, bust-out fraud and mule account opening
Deepfakes and generative AI in onboarding and impersonation
Strong authentication, liveness checks and digital identity

modules.title: Insider Fraud and First-Party Fraud
modules.summary: Fraud committed by employees, contractors and the firm's own customers, how it is concealed, and the controls, culture and investigation practices that reduce it.
objectives: Identify insider fraud risk across roles, systems and third parties
Recognise first-party fraud, including false claims and mule activity
Apply proportionate investigation and response to suspected cases
syllabus: Insider threat: access, opportunity, pressure and rationalisation
Preventive controls: segregation of duties, access reviews and vetting
First-party fraud: false claims, refund abuse and complicit mules
Whistleblowing, investigations and evidence handling

modules.title: Fraud Risk Assessment and Control Design
modules.summary: Building a fraud risk assessment that covers products, channels, customers and third parties, and turning it into a proportionate prevention and detection control framework.
objectives: Conduct a fraud risk assessment across products, channels and customer segments
Design preventive and detective controls proportionate to the assessed risk
Embed fraud risk in product design, change and third-party oversight
syllabus: Inherent risk, control effectiveness and residual risk for fraud
Fraud risk in product design, onboarding journeys and new payment channels
Balancing friction, customer experience and loss prevention
Exercise: fraud risk assessment for a new payment product

modules.title: Transaction Monitoring and Behavioural Analytics
modules.summary: How real-time monitoring, device and behavioural analytics and machine learning detect fraud, how to tune them, and how to evidence their effectiveness.
objectives: Explain rules-based, behavioural and machine learning detection approaches
Tune detection to balance fraud capture, false positives and customer friction
Assess model performance, drift and explainability
syllabus: Real-time payment monitoring, risk scoring and holds
Device intelligence, behavioural biometrics and confirmation of payee checks
Machine learning models: training data, drift and validation
Exercise: interpreting detection performance metrics

modules.title: Customer Warnings, Vulnerability, Reimbursement and Redress
modules.summary: How to intervene effectively with customers at risk, support vulnerable customers, and handle reimbursement, complaints and redress fairly under generic reimbursement frameworks.
objectives: Design warnings and interventions that change customer behaviour
Identify and support customers in vulnerable circumstances
Apply reimbursement and redress decisions consistently and fairly
syllabus: Effective warnings: dynamic, specific and timed to the risk
Vulnerability indicators, escalation and tailored support
Reimbursement models, liability sharing and consumer standard of care
Complaints, redress and learning from outcomes

modules.title: Data Sharing, Governance and Board Reporting
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a fraud governance framework: intelligence and data sharing, collaboration with other firms and law enforcement, management information and board oversight.
objectives: Use intelligence and data sharing lawfully and effectively
Specify fraud management information and key risk indicators for the board
Produce an action plan to strengthen the firm's fraud framework
syllabus: Data sharing between firms, industry bodies, telecoms, platforms and law enforcement
Recovering funds, mule account disruption and suspicious activity reporting
Fraud management information, loss metrics and board reporting
Workshop: fraud framework gap analysis and action plan

related.title: Crypto-Asset Financial Crime: Tracing and Controls for Compliance Teams
related.summary: A nine-module programme equipping compliance teams to detect crypto-asset financial crime, use blockchain analytics, meet travel rule and sanctions obligations, and investigate and report suspicion.

related.title: Financial Crime Compliance in the Age of AI
related.summary: A ten-module programme for MLROs and financial crime teams on the risk-based approach, AI-driven detection, AI-enabled threats and evidencing effectiveness to supervisors.

related.title: MLRO and Financial Crime Leadership
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving MLROs and deputies the tools to lead the firm's financial crime framework, report to the board and handle supervisory inspections.

related.title: Sanctions Compliance
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on designing and running effective sanctions compliance, from ownership and screening to evasion typologies, licensing and breach reporting.

related.title: The EU AML Package: AMLR, AMLD6 and AMLA (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on the EU AML package for supervisors and firms: the AML Regulation single rulebook, AMLD6, AMLA's supervisory model, crypto-asset transfers and transition planning.

related.title: Compliance Officer Academy
related.summary: A ten-module academy giving compliance officers the tools to run an independent, risk-based compliance function and handle supervisory engagement with confidence.
